_doc: P31 type QID -> semantic class, hand-maintained. class: municipality (a separately governed place) | official (an official subdivision of the city) | informal (a recognised name with no administrative standing) | skip (not a division: a negative property, an error, or too generic to classify). The tier NUMBER (first/second division) is NOT stored here - it is derived per city by ordering that city's `official` levels coarse-to-fine, because the same type is a different tier in different cities (Q123705 'neighborhood' is under Amsterdam's stadsdelen but is the only tier Los Angeles has). `byCity` overrides `map` for one city, because a type can be official in one country and not another: Q188509 'suburb' is gazetted in Australia and vernacular everywhere else, and Q4286337 'city district' is Warsaw's dzielnice but Toronto's municipalities dissolved in 1998.

Q106935957.label: City Information System zone in Warsaw
Q106935957.why: Warsaw's MSI is a ZDM wayfinding/signage system, and pl.wikipedia says outright it is neither an administrative division nor a division into osiedla; its boundaries disagree with TERYT. Load-bearing: breadth=1 makes it win both place=quarter and admin=10, so `official` would invent two ~145-unit official tiers under the 18 dzielnice

Q1074955.label: quartiere of Rome
Q1074955.why: second level of Roma Capitale's toponymic division, instituted by municipal deliberation and delimited for statistical and anagrafe use; tiles the urban area. Consistent with Q3575964 'zone of Rome' already being official

Q3301053.label: consolidated city-county
Q3301053.why: a general US governance category - 38 of its 39 instances are whole cities (Philadelphia, Denver, Nashville). On New York's admin=7 it ties Q408804 'borough of New York City' exactly on breadth AND count, so the tiebreak is dict order: any non-skip class would re-label the borough tier at random between builds. NOTE for a wider roster: every other instance also carries 'city in the United States' or 'big city' EXCEPT Philadelphia, which would need its own type mapped

Q11939023.label: populated place nucleus
Q11939023.why: INE/IDESCAT nucli de poblacio - a delimited built-up cluster used for the Nomenclator, statistical, no governance, and it does not tile the municipality. Currently inert anyway: best share 0.22, under MIN_TYPE_SHARE

Q3257686.label: locality
Q3257686.why: bare 'place of human settlement' with no division semantics. Across 12 cities it means four incompatible things: Bogota's governed localidades, Argentine localidades, Australian gazetted localities, and one-off vernacular spots (Kennington Cross, Birkholzaue)

Q3502706.label: suburb of Rome
Q3502706.why: suburbi, the third toponymic level of Roma Capitale, alongside quartieri and zone. Only 6 units - below every guard, so effectively a label

Q2277441.label: osiedle
Q2277441.why: osiedle, Poland's genuine sub-district auxiliary unit - not to be confused with the MSI zones above
